question.problem:
The volumes of soda in cans filled in at a particular factory are normally distributed with a mean of $12\,\text{oz}$ and a standard deviation of $0.4\,\text{oz}.$ Suppose $100$ cans are randomly selected. What is the probability that the mean volume for this sample will be more than $12.1\,\text{oz}?$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.5\,$ | $\,0.9938\,$ | $\,0.9940\,$ | $\,0.9941\,$ | $\,0.9943\,$ | $\,0.9945\,$ |
| $\,2.6\,$ | $\,0.9953\,$ | $\,0.9955\,$ | $\,0.9956\,$ | $\,0.9957\,$ | $\,0.9959\,$ |
| $\,2.7\,$ | $\,0.9965\,$ | $\,0.9966\,$ | $\,0.9967\,$ | $\,0.9968\,$ | $\,0.9969\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

 then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

We're told that the population mean $\mu =12,$ the population standard deviation $\sigma =0.4,$ and that the sample size $n=100.$ Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(12,\frac{{0.4}^{2}}{100}) \\  & ∼N(12,0.0016).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>12.1).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>12.1) & =P(Z>\frac{12.1-12}{\sqrt{0.0016}}) \\  & =P(Z>2.5) \\  & =1-P(Z<2.5) \\  & =1-Φ(2.5)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
Φ(2.5)=0.9938.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>12.1) & =1-Φ(2.5) \\  & =1-0.9938 \\  & =0.0062.\end{aligned}
$$
